title: Dental Caries: An Overview
subtitle: How it develops and what influences it

slides.title: Dental Caries: An Overview
bullets: A brief introduction for educational purposes

slides.title: What Is Caries?
bullets: Gradual acid demineralization of dental hard tissue
Associated with bacterial plaque (biofilm) on the tooth surface
In the early stage, the tooth surface may still be intact
slides.caption: Healthy molar

slides.title: Contributing Factors
bullets: Bacterial plaque on the tooth surface
Sugars and other rapidly fermentable carbohydrates (especially with frequent intake)
Time: the longer plaque remains, the higher the risk
Properties of the tooth itself and of saliva

slides.title: Why Is the Chewing Surface at Greater Risk?
bullets: Fissures (grooves) can be narrow and deep
Toothbrush bristles may not fully penetrate them
These areas therefore need particular attention during cleaning
slides.caption: Fissures on the chewing surface

slides.title: When Caries Progresses Deeper
bullets: It may spread from enamel into dentin
Sensitivity may increase via the dentinal tubules
Only a dentist decides on treatment, after an examination
slides.caption: Position of enamel, dentin and pulp

slides.title: Basics of Prevention
bullets: Brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste
Reducing how much and how often sweets are consumed
Cleaning the interdental spaces
Dental check-ups at the intervals recommended by a dentist

slides.title: Key Points
bullets: Caries is a process of acid-driven demineralization
Biofilm and sugars are the main factors
Prevention starts with simple daily habits
Diagnosis and treatment are the dentist’s responsibility

options: Only a change in tooth color
Filling of the tooth with new cells
Demineralization of the tooth by acids

quiz.explanation: Biofilm and rapidly fermentable carbohydrates are among the main factors.

quiz.q: Why are fissures difficult to clean?
options: They are located in the pulp
They can be narrow and deep
quiz.explanation: Toothbrush bristles may not reach into narrow grooves.

quiz.q: Who makes the decision on caries treatment?
quiz.explanation: Diagnosis and treatment are determined after a dental examination.
